svg.title: Three identity checks close three different protection gaps in one normal fix
svg.desc: A left-to-right timeline of one normal fix. Gap A lies between the unprotected hash-chain observation and taking the BCB mutex; identity recheck 1 closes it by comparing the BCB VPID again under the mutex. Gap B lies between hit or miss preparation and the common convergence point; identity recheck 2 compares the BCB identity with the identity stored in the page header. Gap C is the borrowed-use period; identity recheck 3 revalidates the BCB and page header at unfix before the global fix count is decremented. Each check validates a different observation under different protection, so none of them can replace another.
svg.text: One normal fix, three protection gaps, three identity checks
WHAT MAY HAVE CHANGED SINCE THE LAST OBSERVATION
Gap A: candidate seen without protection
Hash chain walked before the BCB mutex is held.
A victimizer may unlink this BCB and rebind it
to another VPID in that window.
Gap B: bytes prepared, not cross-checked
Hit: resident bytes found. Miss: bytes just read
from the DWB image or the data volume. Control
block and page image could still disagree.
Gap C: borrowed use
The caller holds latch, fcnt, and holder, then
calls unfix with a PAGE_PTR. The pointer is an
address into a reusable frame, not an identity.
time
lock BCB
hit and miss converge
unfix
WHICH OBSERVATION EACH CHECK VALIDATES, AND UNDER WHAT PROTECTION
Identity recheck 1: under the BCB mutex
Is bufptr->vpid still the requested VPID?
Fail: unlock this BCB and walk the chain again.
closes Gap A; protection: BCB mutex
Identity recheck 2: at convergence
BCB vpid equals page header volid/pageid?
Fail: no PAGE_PTR; new BCB back to the invalid list.
closes Gap B; protection: BCB mutex, hit or miss
Identity recheck 3: while releasing
BCB identity non-null and header still agrees,
then holder minus one, then global fcnt minus one.
closes Gap C; debug assertion under the BCB mutex
Each check guards a different gap under different protection. Removing one leaves that gap unguarded; it does not make the other two redundant.
